title: Trailing slash directory paths in the daemon namespace
scope: Existing-object resolution accepts a trailing slash and requires the resolved object to be a directory; all-slash paths resolve to the World root
A final symlink is followed when a trailing slash requires directory traversal, including lstat and link-attribute operations
File, dangling-link, symlink-to-file, and looping-link paths with a trailing slash are rejected while preserving generic raw-RPC wire error code 1
Parent-based create, mkdir, remove, rename and link destination paths, O_CREAT paths, and revision diff cursor paths continue to reject trailing slashes
Raw paths retain the 4096-byte limit and components retain the 255-byte limit; a directory hint ending in slash falls back to its canonical physical path before an inode RPC child is appended
Regression coverage includes modern and legacy storage, revisions, forks, modern GC and reopen
explicit_exclusions: This validates C++ Namespace and raw daemon RPC behavior only; it does not claim native filesystem mount semantics or a new mount capability
No new typed error or RPC error mapping is claimed; existing generic runtime-error mapping is preserved
Trailing slashes remain unsupported for parent-path mutation parsing and revision diff cursor parsing
